newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Polling gets off to dull start in Karachi.
newsitem.headline: Polling gets off to dull start in Karachi.

text.p: Polling stations in Pakistan's southern port city of Karachi were virtually deserted when they opened for national elections on Monday, witnesses said.

"Unlike the past, there is little public enthusiasm today. I remember there used to be long queues of voters even an hour before the polling started. But today there are hardly any," said Mehjabeen Ghazanfar, an assistant presiding officer at a polling station in Karachi's District East.
At most polling stations, party workers did not show up until 7:00 a.m. (0200 GMT), when voting was due to begin.

"We are still waiting for the tables and other election stuff, while the MQM (Mohajir National Movement) people have already set up their stall," complained a Pakistan Muslim League (PML) candidate at a District South polling station.
Another PML worker, Mazhar Hussain, said voter turn-out would be low because of the Moslem holy fasting month of Ramadan and a general lack of enthusiasm during the election campaign.
Troops guarded the polling stations, while paramilitary rangers patrolled the streets of this volatile city.
About 56.5 million Pakistanis aged 21 and over are eligible to vote in the elections for a new 217-seat National Assembly (lower house) and four provincial assemblies.
The polling stations will stay open until 4:00 p.m. (1100 GMT), with results expected in the evening.
The main fight is between the PML and former prime minister Benazir Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party.
In overnight violence, two supporters of the breakaway MQM-Haqiqi faction were wounded by gunfire in Moosa Colony of District Central, considered a bastion of the mainstream Karachi-based MQM.
Tension between the rival factions has run high during the election campaign and at least four people were killed.
The MQM speaks for Urdu-speaking people who migrated to Pakistan from India at Partition in 1947 and their descendants.
